CRITICAL BUG FOUND & FIXED in backend/pensees.py: PenseeIn model had `date: Optional[date]` where the field name shadowed the `from datetime import date` import → Pydantic 2.13 resolved the annotation as `None`, making the API return 422 'none_required' whenever the frontend sent `date`. rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: /app/backend/pensees.py defined `PenseeIn.date: Optional[date] = None` where field name `date` was identical to the imported `datetime.date` class. Under Pydantic 2.13 (used here), the annotation lookup resolved `date` to a self-referential/unresolvable name, effectively typing the field as `Optional[None]` → the validator only accepted `None` and rejected any string with error `none_required` (HTTP 422). REPRO: `curl -X POST /api/pensees -d '{"theme":"x","date":"2026-01-15"}'` returns 422 `{'type':'none_required','loc':['body','date'],'msg':'Input should be None'}`. Any frontend POST from /media/pensees was 100% broken since the modal always sends today's date. FIX: renamed the import to `from datetime import date as _date` and updated the three usage sites (`Optional[_date]` annotation, `_date.today()` in `today()` and `create_pensee`). Verified: POST with date now returns 201; POST without date defaults to server today; POST with `date:null` still allowed. Same fix pattern recommended to avoid recurrence.
